title: Box Corner to Corner: 3D Distance Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
A box is 12 cm long, 4 cm wide and 3 cm tall. A 13 cm pencil will not lie flat inside it, but tilted from one bottom corner to the opposite top corner it fits exactly. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 11, Introduction to Three Dimensional Geometry) we find out why, and build the distance formula in three dimensions.

You will watch the lid of the box lift live while the corner to corner line grows from 12.65 to exactly 13, then use Pythagoras twice: once across the floor, once straight up. We turn that into PQ = root of the three changes squared, see the distance from the origin, compare it with the 2D formula, and learn why PQ always equals QP. Then a worked example, the exam trap about minus signs, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.

In this video:
0:00 Will the pencil fit in the box?
0:35 Three coordinates, and the lid lifts live
1:04 Pythagoras twice
1:47 The distance formula for any two points
2:34 2D vs 3D: one square per direction
3:06 Does the order of P and Q matter?
3:30 Worked example
4:10 Exam trap: minus signs
4:31 Where it is asked
4:41 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:15 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 80): Intuitive Idea of Limits. Walk halfway to a wall, then half of what is left, again and again. Do you ever touch it?
